q: A screen shows 2000 products. What does a ScrollView do with them?
options: Mounts only the rows near the screen
Mounts only the 16 rows you can see
why: A ScrollView renders all its children at once. That slows the start and uses memory. A FlatList mounts only the rows near the screen.

q: With the default windowSize of 21, a FlatList keeps 21 rows mounted.
why: No. windowSize counts screens, not rows. 21 means 10 screens above, the screen you see and 10 below. With 16 rows per screen that is hundreds of rows.

q: Which changes make a blank area less likely when you fling a FlatList? Pick all that fit.
options: Give getItemLayout when every row has the same height
Use the index as the key
why: Lighter rows and a known row height are free help. A bigger window costs memory. The key does not change how fast rows are made, and the index is a bad key for a list that changes.

q: You select a row and change selectedId in state, but the row colour does not change. What is the fix?
options: Change the key to the index
why: FlatList is a PureComponent. It only runs again when its props change. Anything the rows depend on outside data goes in extraData.

q: Put these in the order they happen when a FlatList opens and you start to scroll (defaults).
items: More rows are added in batches of 10, about 50 ms apart
The window fills around the screen
You scroll, and far rows are unmounted while new rows are mounted
why: The first render is small so the screen opens fast. Batches fill the window. Scrolling then moves the window.

q: Rows in a FlatList are checked by their own state. After you delete the first item, the checkmark moves to the wrong row because the key was the ____.
why: With the index as the key, key 0 now belongs to a different item, so React keeps the old state. Use a key that belongs to the item, like its id.
